plain_description.what: On the clean version-2 evaluation set (5,907 questions x 18 models), it measures how much of the variation in question difficulty is explained by the anchor-free tree's cells, compared with random cells of the same size drawn within each source benchmark. A secondary check looked at 7 cells where model rankings flip.
plain_description.why: If cells are only topics, they might not matter for evaluation. If they also group questions by difficulty, that helps explain why per-cell rankings differ.
plain_description.information: A clear excess over random cells shows the cells capture real difficulty structure. No excess would mean cells are difficulty-neutral labels. Result: done, valid. The cells are difficulty strata: they explain 23% of difficulty variation against at most about 8% for random cells. Per-source k-means cells do at least as well (24%, descriptive), so this does not show the tree beats k-means. The 7-flip-cell check is only a consistency check, not evidence of more than one ability dimension.
